مَضْرُوبٌ : see ضَرْبٌ and ضَرِيبٌ, the latter in two places. Dhu-r-Rummeh says, speaking of a cake of bread (خُبْزَة), “وَمَضْرُوبَةٍ فِى غَيْرِ ذَنْبٍ بَرِيئَةِ
كَسَرْتُ لِأْصْحَابِى عَلَى عَجَلٍ كَسْرَا
” [Many a thing (meaning many a cake of bread) beaten for no offence, free from blame, I have broken for my companions in haste, with a vigorous breaking]. (TA, after explaining the phrase أَضْرَبَ الخُبْزُ [q. v.].) ―
-b2- Also (assumed tropical:) Staying, abiding, or remaining, [fixed, or settled,] in a tent, or house. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
